1	# audit-chain
2	
3	Per-tenant audit log where every entry is chained to its predecessor, so a reader can verify a tenant history offline and pinpoint the first broken index.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	    python3 -m pip install -e .
12	
13	## Run
14	
15	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit append <tenant> --payload <json-file>
16	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit verify <tenant>
17	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit recover
18	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit rotate
19	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit compact [--max-segments N]
20	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit archive <archive-dir>
21	    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit export <tenant> --start N --end M > proof.json
22	    python3 -m audit_chain verify-proof proof.json [--tenant T] [--start N] [--end M]
23	
24	`--path` is either a single JSON-lines log file or a segment store
25	(directory); the first `rotate` migrates an existing file into a store at the
26	same path. Exit codes: `0` success, `1` verification found a broken entry
27	(including a tampered cache, manifest or sealed window), `2` any other error
28	(missing file, bad/half-written line, corrupt chain, bad payload type,
29	illegal proof range, lock contention, path/permission errors). Error paths
30	print nothing. `verify-proof` never opens the log and keeps its output to
31	the success case: exactly one compact JSON line with the keys `ok`,
32	`first_bad` and `count` (sorted, no extra whitespace, one trailing
33	newline). A broken proof exits `1` silently; any other failure exits `2`
34	silently.
35	
36	## Public interface
37	
38	`audit_chain.Chain(path)` opens the log file.
39	- `append(tenant, payload) -> dict` appends and returns the stored entry.
40	- `entries(tenant) -> list[dict]` returns entries in insertion order.
41	- `verify(tenant) -> dict` re-derives the chain and reports the first bad index.
42	- `head(tenant) -> str | None` returns the newest digest.
43	- `export_range(tenant, start, end) -> dict` builds an offline proof for the
44	  half-open interval `[start, end)` (see below).
45	
46	Additional entry points:
47	- `recover() -> {"truncated_bytes": n}` truncates a half-written tail line
48	  left by a killed process; complete but broken records are never repaired.
49	- `rotate()` seals the active segment and starts a new one.
50	- `compact(max_segments=2) -> {"segments": n}` merges old segments.
51	- `archive(archive_dir) -> {"archived": n}` migrates every sealed segment
52	  to the caller-specified archive directory, online.
53	
54	`audit_chain.verify_proof(proof, *, tenant=None, start=None, end=None)`
55	verifies an exported proof with the public digest function alone; it never
56	touches the log.
57	
58	Two more offline entry points work purely on proof objects (no log):
59	- `audit_chain.combine_proofs(left, right) -> dict` splices two proofs of the
60	  same tenant whose intervals meet end-to-start (`left["end"] ==
61	  right["start"]`) into one ordinary proof covering the union
62	  `[left["start"], right["end"])`. It is associative, re-verifies both inputs
63	  and the result, and the combined proof checks out through `verify_proof`
64	  after the log itself has been compressed or deleted. A non-dict argument is
65	  `TypeError`; a side that is not a valid exporting proof or does not verify,
66	  or a tenant mismatch / gap / overlap / reversed order, is `ValueError`.
67	- `audit_chain.verify_proofs(proofs) -> list[dict]` verifies a batch and
68	  returns one verdict per proof, in input order, each with the same shape as
69	  the on-chain verdict. A tampered proof yields an `ok=False` verdict with the
70	  real global bad index without interrupting the rest. An empty list is
71	  `ValueError`; the argument or an element that is not a dict is `TypeError`.
72	
73	`audit_chain.extend_proof(proof, path) -> dict` continues an exported (or
74	combined) proof against the store at `path`: the result is an ordinary proof

80	reversed or non-verifying proof, or one whose end lies beyond the log's
81	intact prefix, is `ValueError`; a missing log is `FileNotFoundError`.

85	consecutive shards of at most `window` records each, and every shard is an

87	the whole-interval proof with `combine_proofs`). The shards tile the
88	interval exactly — end of one is the start of the next, no gap, no overlap.
89	The returned iterator produces shards lazily, so memory tracks a single
90	window, never the interval length; the snapshot lock is held for the whole
91	stream, so every shard describes the same complete prefix even if other
92	processes append, rotate, merge or archive meanwhile. The export writes

94	and a fresh re-export yields the byte-identical shard sequence. A
95	non-positive or non-integer `window`, an empty or reversed interval, and
96	non-integer or out-of-bounds endpoints raise `ValueError`.

98	`audit_chain.verify_proof_stream(shards, *, tenant=None, start=None, end=None)`
99	consumes an iterable of shards (for example the iterator above) and returns
100	`{"shards": [...], "total": {...}}`: one verdict per shard in input order
101	plus the whole-interval verdict, each in the `verify_proof` verdict shape.

104	tampered or malformed shard yields a corrupted verdict without interrupting
105	the remaining shards. An empty shard stream or a non-dict element raises
106	`TypeError`; a gap or overlap between shards raises `ValueError`.
107	`audit_chain.ShardVerifier(tenant=..., start=..., end=...)` is the
108	incremental form: `.check(shard)` returns each shard's verdict as it is fed,
109	`.finish()` returns the whole-interval verdict.
110	
111	`Chain.export_shards_dir(tenant, start, end, window, directory)` persists
112	the same windowed export as a shard directory: one file per shard
113	(`shard-00000000.json`, ...), each byte-identical to the corresponding
114	in-memory shard, plus a self-authenticating `manifest.json` — one compact
115	JSON line with a trailing newline, recording in shard order every shard's
116	file name, index interval and byte sha256. It returns `{"shards": n}` with
117	`n` the number of completely persisted shards. Every file is committed
118	with a temp-file write + fsync + atomic rename and the manifest is
119	re-committed as each shard lands, so a process killed in any commit
120	window leaves the directory at the old or the new committed state. Calling
121	it again on the same directory resumes the export: shards the manifest
122	already vouches for are authenticated in place and never rewritten, only
123	the missing ones are produced. A target that is not a directory, an
124	unparseable or tampered manifest, a manifest describing a different
125	export, or an existing shard that does not match the manifest raises
126	`ValueError`; argument type errors raise `TypeError`.

129	shard directory for offline verification: it authenticates the shard
130	against the manifest and never opens the log or any other shard. A
131	missing directory, manifest or shard file raises `FileNotFoundError`; an
132	unparseable manifest or shard, a shard that does not match the manifest,
133	or an out-of-range index raises `ValueError`. The shards of a directory
134	splice back into the whole-interval conclusion with `combine_proofs` /
135	`verify_proof_stream`, item-wise identical to a one-shot export of the
136	same interval.
137	
138	### Online archiving
139	
140	`archive(archive_dir)` moves every sealed segment out of the hot store
141	into the caller-specified archive directory while the log stays online.
142	The self-authenticating manifest records the archive location and keeps
143	each migrated segment's byte-window material, so later opens need no
144	extra arguments: append, query, verify, rotate, compact, recover and
145	export all work unchanged across the hot and archive tiers, per-tenant
146	indices stay continuous from zero, rotation order is untouched, and a
147	post-archive verify reports exactly the first bad index a pre-archive
148	verify would. Migrated segments no longer occupy the hot directory. The
149	migration is serialized with appends and merges by the same lock, so a
150	concurrent reader always sees one complete prefix and a writer is never
151	starved out; a process killed mid-migration reopens onto either the
152	pre-archive or the complete post-archive topology -- staged copies,
153	orphans and hot duplicates are reaped deterministically, and no segment
154	is ever half moved or left in both tiers. Archiving a damaged log, a
155	legacy unsegmented file, or a location that conflicts with the recorded
156	one raises `ValueError`.
157	
158	### Snapshot consistency
159	
160	`verify`, `entries` and `head` each run under a shared process lock and read
161	one fixed unit list in one ordered pass, while append/rotate/compact/recover
162	run under an exclusive lock. A single call therefore always observes one
163	complete prefix — the topology immediately before or immediately after a
164	rotation or merge — never mixed segments, a duplicated run or a skipped run.
165	
166	### Incremental, constant-read-amplification verification
167	
168	Concurrent appenders to one log are serialized by a cross-platform file lock
169	(`flock` on POSIX, `LockFileEx` on Windows), so records always link strictly
170	with continuous zero-based per-tenant indices. Each sealed segment keeps
171	byte-level verification material (size + sha256 per source segment, retained
172	through compaction). A repeat verify hashes only newly appended bytes plus a
173	small amount of sidecar material — never the whole file, and never a sealed
174	byte window on the hot path. The manifest is self-authenticating and the
175	verify cache is authenticated; tampering with the cache, the manifest or a
176	sealed window is reported as corruption (`ok=False`) with the real first bad
177	index rather than a pass. Tenants stay isolated: one tenant's damage never
178	changes another tenant's verdict.
179	
180	### Offline range proofs
181	
182	`export_range(tenant, start, end)` returns a self-contained proof for a
183	contiguous interval. It contains only the interval's chained records and the
184	strictly-increasing cross-segment window anchors (offset/size/sha256) needed
185	to attach them; no out-of-interval payload is included. An independent reader
186	recomputes every digest, checks predecessor links, indices, offsets and the
187	window chain using `verify_proof` (and the public digest) alone. Damage
188	outside the interval cannot affect its conclusion. Empty or reversed
189	intervals, non-integer or out-of-bounds ranges raise `ValueError`; a tenant
190	with no history returns a verifiable empty-history proof for `(0, 0)`.
191	
192	Two proofs exported from the same tenant can be joined with
193	`combine_proofs`: when their indices meet end-to-start the result is the same
194	kind of proof over the union, independently verifiable, and associating three
195	pieces pairwise gives the same conclusion as one proof over the whole range.
196	This holds with endpoints on segment boundaries, across segments merged by
197	compaction, and across the cross-segment window chain; it stays verifiable
198	after the log is compacted, corrupted or deleted. `verify_proofs` verifies
199	many proofs at once, one verdict each in order.
200	
201	An exported proof can later be continued with `extend_proof(proof, path)`:
202	the extension reads only the records appended after the proof's end — under
203	the same shared lock as every other read, so a concurrent append, rotation,
204	merge or archive migration yields a result for one complete prefix, never a
205	mixed topology — and splices the increment on with `combine_proofs`. The
206	result is an ordinary proof to the current prefix; it writes nothing to the
207	store, so an interrupted extension leaves no temp files or half-built state
208	and can simply be retried.
209	
210	### Export cost
211	
212	Exporting (and extending, and splicing, and batch verification) costs work
213	proportional to the interval or increment, not to total history length. With a warm, authenticated verify
214	cache an export opens only the segment files that hold an interval record and
215	reads no others; records in sealed segments are anchored straight from the
216	signed manifest material, so sealed bytes are never hashed, and records in the
217	still-growing tail are anchored over small windows containing only the
218	interval's own lines. A never-verified or altered store transparently falls
219	back to a full ordered byte scan with identical conclusions. Sharded export
220	(`export_shards`) inherits the same cost model shard by shard: production
221	memory tracks a single window, and digest work and read volume track the
222	interval, never the history length. Persisting the shards
223	(`export_shards_dir`) keeps that model: a resumed export reads only the
224	missing increment, and `open_shard` reads only the shard it returns.
225	
226	### Crash recovery
227	
228	Every commit is a temp-file write + fsync + atomic rename, and a merge
229	publishes its bytes before swapping the manifest and only removes old
230	segments afterwards. A process hard-killed in any window (partial write,
231	flush/fsync, segment rename, manifest replacement, old-segment deletion)

236	
237	## Tests
238	
239	    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
240	
241	The suite includes a real-kill crash-injection matrix (separate processes
242	hard-killed at each commit window), concurrent snapshot-consistency stress,
243	tamper-evidence tests and offline-proof tests.
244	
245	## Limits
246	
247	Payloads must be JSON-serialisable.
248	No network service and no remote anchoring.

# audit-chain

Per-tenant audit log where every entry is chained to its predecessor, so a reader can verify a tenant history offline and pinpoint the first broken index.

## Requirements

Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.

## Install

    python3 -m pip install -e .

## Run

    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit append <tenant> --payload <json-file>
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit verify <tenant>
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit recover
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit rotate
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit compact [--max-segments N]
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit archive <archive-dir>
    python3 -m audit_chain --path ./audit export <tenant> --start N --end M > proof.json
    python3 -m audit_chain verify-proof proof.json [--tenant T] [--start N] [--end M]

`--path` is either a single JSON-lines log file or a segment store
(directory); the first `rotate` migrates an existing file into a store at the
same path. Exit codes: `0` success, `1` verification found a broken entry
(including a tampered cache, manifest or sealed window), `2` any other error
(missing file, bad/half-written line, corrupt chain, bad payload type,
illegal proof range, lock contention, path/permission errors). Error paths
print nothing. `verify-proof` never opens the log and keeps its output to
the success case: exactly one compact JSON line with the keys `ok`,
`first_bad` and `count` (sorted, no extra whitespace, one trailing
newline). A broken proof exits `1` silently; any other failure exits `2`
silently.

## Public interface

`audit_chain.Chain(path)` opens the log file.
- `append(tenant, payload) -> dict` appends and returns the stored entry.
- `entries(tenant) -> list[dict]` returns entries in insertion order.
- `verify(tenant) -> dict` re-derives the chain and reports the first bad index.
- `head(tenant) -> str | None` returns the newest digest.
- `export_range(tenant, start, end) -> dict` builds an offline proof for the
  half-open interval `[start, end)` (see below).

Additional entry points:
- `recover() -> {"truncated_bytes": n}` truncates a half-written tail line
  left by a killed process; complete but broken records are never repaired.
- `rotate()` seals the active segment and starts a new one.
- `compact(max_segments=2) -> {"segments": n}` merges old segments.
- `archive(archive_dir) -> {"archived": n}` migrates every sealed segment
  to the caller-specified archive directory, online.

`audit_chain.verify_proof(proof, *, tenant=None, start=None, end=None)`
verifies an exported proof with the public digest function alone; it never
touches the log.

Two more offline entry points work purely on proof objects (no log):
- `audit_chain.combine_proofs(left, right) -> dict` splices two proofs of the
  same tenant whose intervals meet end-to-start (`left["end"] ==
  right["start"]`) into one ordinary proof covering the union
  `[left["start"], right["end"])`. It is associative, re-verifies both inputs
  and the result, and the combined proof checks out through `verify_proof`
  after the log itself has been compressed or deleted. A non-dict argument is
  `TypeError`; a side that is not a valid exporting proof or does not verify,
  or a tenant mismatch / gap / overlap / reversed order, is `ValueError`.
- `audit_chain.verify_proofs(proofs) -> list[dict]` verifies a batch and
  returns one verdict per proof, in input order, each with the same shape as
  the on-chain verdict. A tampered proof yields an `ok=False` verdict with the
  real global bad index without interrupting the rest. An empty list is
  `ValueError`; the argument or an element that is not a dict is `TypeError`.

`audit_chain.extend_proof(proof, path) -> dict` continues an exported (or
combined) proof against the store at `path`: the result is an ordinary proof
covering `[proof["start"], n)`, where `n` is the tenant's record count at the
moment of the read. Only the records appended after `proof["end"]` are read
and chained, so the cost tracks the increment, never the history length; the
increment is spliced on with `combine_proofs`. With no new records the result
is equivalent to the input. A non-dict proof is `TypeError`; a malformed,
reversed or non-verifying proof, or one whose end lies beyond the log's
intact prefix, is `ValueError`; a missing log is `FileNotFoundError`.

`Chain.export_shards(tenant, start, end, window)` streams one interval
export as window-sized shards: the interval `[start, end)` is cut into
consecutive shards of at most `window` records each, and every shard is an
ordinary offline proof (verifiable with `verify_proof`, re-combinable into
the whole-interval proof with `combine_proofs`). The shards tile the
interval exactly — end of one is the start of the next, no gap, no overlap.
The returned iterator produces shards lazily, so memory tracks a single
window, never the interval length; the snapshot lock is held for the whole
stream, so every shard describes the same complete prefix even if other
processes append, rotate, merge or archive meanwhile. The export writes
nothing to the store: an interrupted production leaves no temp files behind,
and a fresh re-export yields the byte-identical shard sequence. A
non-positive or non-integer `window`, an empty or reversed interval, and
non-integer or out-of-bounds endpoints raise `ValueError`.

`audit_chain.verify_proof_stream(shards, *, tenant=None, start=None, end=None)`
consumes an iterable of shards (for example the iterator above) and returns
`{"shards": [...], "total": {...}}`: one verdict per shard in input order
plus the whole-interval verdict, each in the `verify_proof` verdict shape.
The total is item-wise identical to the offline verdict of a single export
over the same interval, with `first_bad` on the real first bad record; a
tampered or malformed shard yields a corrupted verdict without interrupting
the remaining shards. An empty shard stream or a non-dict element raises
`TypeError`; a gap or overlap between shards raises `ValueError`.
`audit_chain.ShardVerifier(tenant=..., start=..., end=...)` is the
incremental form: `.check(shard)` returns each shard's verdict as it is fed,
`.finish()` returns the whole-interval verdict.

`Chain.export_shards_dir(tenant, start, end, window, directory)` persists
the same windowed export as a shard directory: one file per shard
(`shard-00000000.json`, ...), each byte-identical to the corresponding
in-memory shard, plus a self-authenticating `manifest.json` — one compact
JSON line with a trailing newline, recording in shard order every shard's
file name, index interval and byte sha256. It returns `{"shards": n}` with
`n` the number of completely persisted shards. Every file is committed
with a temp-file write + fsync + atomic rename and the manifest is
re-committed as each shard lands, so a process killed in any commit
window leaves the directory at the old or the new committed state. Calling
it again on the same directory resumes the export: shards the manifest
already vouches for are authenticated in place and never rewritten, only
the missing ones are produced. A target that is not a directory, an
unparseable or tampered manifest, a manifest describing a different
export, or an existing shard that does not match the manifest raises
`ValueError`; argument type errors raise `TypeError`.

`audit_chain.open_shard(directory, index)` reads one shard back out of a
shard directory for offline verification: it authenticates the shard
against the manifest and never opens the log or any other shard. A
missing directory, manifest or shard file raises `FileNotFoundError`; an
unparseable manifest or shard, a shard that does not match the manifest,
or an out-of-range index raises `ValueError`. The shards of a directory
splice back into the whole-interval conclusion with `combine_proofs` /
`verify_proof_stream`, item-wise identical to a one-shot export of the
same interval.

### Online archiving

`archive(archive_dir)` moves every sealed segment out of the hot store
into the caller-specified archive directory while the log stays online.
The self-authenticating manifest records the archive location and keeps
each migrated segment's byte-window material, so later opens need no
extra arguments: append, query, verify, rotate, compact, recover and
export all work unchanged across the hot and archive tiers, per-tenant
indices stay continuous from zero, rotation order is untouched, and a
post-archive verify reports exactly the first bad index a pre-archive
verify would. Migrated segments no longer occupy the hot directory. The
migration is serialized with appends and merges by the same lock, so a
concurrent reader always sees one complete prefix and a writer is never
starved out; a process killed mid-migration reopens onto either the
pre-archive or the complete post-archive topology -- staged copies,
orphans and hot duplicates are reaped deterministically, and no segment
is ever half moved or left in both tiers. Archiving a damaged log, a
legacy unsegmented file, or a location that conflicts with the recorded
one raises `ValueError`.

### Snapshot consistency

`verify`, `entries` and `head` each run under a shared process lock and read
one fixed unit list in one ordered pass, while append/rotate/compact/recover
run under an exclusive lock. A single call therefore always observes one
complete prefix — the topology immediately before or immediately after a
rotation or merge — never mixed segments, a duplicated run or a skipped run.

### Incremental, constant-read-amplification verification

Concurrent appenders to one log are serialized by a cross-platform file lock
(`flock` on POSIX, `LockFileEx` on Windows), so records always link strictly
with continuous zero-based per-tenant indices. Each sealed segment keeps
byte-level verification material (size + sha256 per source segment, retained
through compaction). A repeat verify hashes only newly appended bytes plus a

verify cache is authenticated; tampering with the cache, the manifest or a
sealed window is reported as corruption (`ok=False`) with the real first bad
index rather than a pass. Tenants stay isolated: one tenant's damage never
changes another tenant's verdict.

### Offline range proofs

`export_range(tenant, start, end)` returns a self-contained proof for a
contiguous interval. It contains only the interval's chained records and the
strictly-increasing cross-segment window anchors (offset/size/sha256) needed
to attach them; no out-of-interval payload is included. An independent reader
recomputes every digest, checks predecessor links, indices, offsets and the
window chain using `verify_proof` (and the public digest) alone. Damage
outside the interval cannot affect its conclusion. Empty or reversed
intervals, non-integer or out-of-bounds ranges raise `ValueError`; a tenant
with no history returns a verifiable empty-history proof for `(0, 0)`.

Two proofs exported from the same tenant can be joined with
`combine_proofs`: when their indices meet end-to-start the result is the same
kind of proof over the union, independently verifiable, and associating three
pieces pairwise gives the same conclusion as one proof over the whole range.
This holds with endpoints on segment boundaries, across segments merged by
compaction, and across the cross-segment window chain; it stays verifiable
after the log is compacted, corrupted or deleted. `verify_proofs` verifies
many proofs at once, one verdict each in order.

An exported proof can later be continued with `extend_proof(proof, path)`:
the extension reads only the records appended after the proof's end — under
the same shared lock as every other read, so a concurrent append, rotation,
merge or archive migration yields a result for one complete prefix, never a
mixed topology — and splices the increment on with `combine_proofs`. The
result is an ordinary proof to the current prefix; it writes nothing to the
store, so an interrupted extension leaves no temp files or half-built state
and can simply be retried.

### Export cost

Exporting (and extending, and splicing, and batch verification) costs work
proportional to the interval or increment, not to total history length. With a warm, authenticated verify
cache an export opens only the segment files that hold an interval record and
reads no others; records in sealed segments are anchored straight from the
signed manifest material, so sealed bytes are never hashed, and records in the
still-growing tail are anchored over small windows containing only the
interval's own lines. A never-verified or altered store transparently falls

(`export_shards`) inherits the same cost model shard by shard: production
memory tracks a single window, and digest work and read volume track the
interval, never the history length. Persisting the shards
(`export_shards_dir`) keeps that model: a resumed export reads only the
missing increment, and `open_shard` reads only the shard it returns.

### Crash recovery

Every commit is a temp-file write + fsync + atomic rename, and a merge
publishes its bytes before swapping the manifest and only removes old
segments afterwards. A process hard-killed in any window (partial write,
flush/fsync, segment rename, manifest replacement, old-segment deletion)
reopens onto either the old topology or the complete new one: a migration
backup is adopted, a staged directory / orphan segment / residual temp file
is reaped by the next writer, and a half-written tail line keeps its bad-line
semantics until `recover()` truncates it.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

The suite includes a real-kill crash-injection matrix (separate processes
hard-killed at each commit window), concurrent snapshot-consistency stress,
tamper-evidence tests and offline-proof tests.

## Limits

Payloads must be JSON-serialisable.
No network service and no remote anchoring.

2	
3	A shard directory holds one file per shard -- ``shard-00000000.json``,
4	``shard-00000001.json``, ... -- where each file's bytes are exactly the
5	canonical JSON of the corresponding in-memory shard proof, plus a
6	self-authenticating ``manifest.json``: one compact JSON line terminated
7	by a single newline, recording in shard order every shard's file name,
8	index interval and the sha256 of its file bytes, sealed by an
9	authentication tag over the whole manifest.
10	
11	Every file is committed with a temp-file write + fsync + atomic rename
12	and the manifest is re-committed as each shard lands, so a process
13	killed in any commit window leaves the directory at either the old or
14	the new committed state -- never a half-written shard. A later export
15	call on the same directory resumes from the committed manifest: shards
16	the manifest vouches for are authenticated in place and never rewritten,
17	only the missing ones are produced.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import contextlib
23	import hashlib
24	import json
25	import os
26	from typing import Any
27	
28	from . import record as rec
29	from . import storage as st
30	
31	MANIFEST_NAME = "manifest.json"
32	SHARD_PREFIX = "shard-"
33	SHARD_SUFFIX = ".json"
34	MANIFEST_VERSION = 1
35	_CHUNK = 1 << 20
36	_HEX64 = frozenset("0123456789abcdef")
37	
38	
39	def shard_name(index: int) -> str:
40	    return f"{SHARD_PREFIX}{index:08d}{SHARD_SUFFIX}"
41	
42	
43	def shard_count(start: int, end: int, window: int) -> int:
44	    """Shards needed to tile ``[start, end)`` with pieces of ``window``."""
45	    return -(-(end - start) // window)
46	
47	
48	def shard_slot(start: int, end: int, window: int, index: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
49	    """The index interval shard ``index`` of the tiling must cover."""
50	    lo = start + index * window
51	    return lo, min(lo + window, end)
52	
53	
54	def shard_bytes(shard: dict) -> bytes:
55	    """The canonical on-disk bytes of one shard: compact JSON, nothing else."""
56	    return rec.canonical_json(shard).encode("utf-8")
57	
58	
59	def file_digest(path: str) -> str:
60	    """Streaming sha256 of a file; memory stays bounded for any file size."""
61	    h = hashlib.sha256()
62	    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
63	        while True:
64	            chunk = handle.read(_CHUNK)
65	            if not chunk:
66	                return h.hexdigest()
67	            h.update(chunk)
68	
69	
70	def write_shard(directory: str, name: str, raw: bytes) -> None:
71	    """Commit one shard file (temp file + fsync + atomic rename)."""
72	    st.atomic_write_bytes(directory, name, raw)
73	
74	
75	def save_manifest(directory: str, manifest: dict) -> None:
76	    """Sign and commit the manifest as one compact JSON line + newline."""
77	    st.atomic_write_text(directory, MANIFEST_NAME, manifest_text(manifest))
78	
79	
80	def manifest_text(manifest: dict) -> str:
81	    return rec.canonical_json(sign_manifest(manifest)) + "\n"
82	
83	
84	def sign_manifest(manifest: dict) -> dict:
85	    """A manifest copy carrying its authentication tag."""
86	    signed = _manifest_body(manifest)
87	    signed["tag"] = hashlib.sha256(
88	        rec.canonical_json(signed).encode("utf-8")
89	    ).hexdigest()
90	    return signed
91	
92	
93	def load_manifest(directory: str) -> dict:
94	    """Read and authenticate the shard directory's manifest.
95	
96	    ``FileNotFoundError`` when the manifest is absent; ``ValueError``
97	    when it cannot be parsed, is structurally invalid, or its
98	    authentication tag does not match its content.
99	    """
100	    with open(os.path.join(directory, MANIFEST_NAME), "rb") as handle:
101	        raw = handle.read()
102	    try:

    def export_shards(

        length; with a warm, authenticated verify cache only the units
        covering the interval are opened and no sealed byte is hashed,

        one ordered counting scan plus the bounded collection, with
        identical shards). The snapshot lock is taken at call time and

        concurrent append, rotation, merge or archive migration blocks
        meanwhile, so every shard describes the same complete prefix --

        production leaves no temp files or half-built state in the
        store directory, and a fresh re-export of the same interval and
        window yields the byte-identical shard sequence.

"""Persisted shard directories (export_shards_dir) and random access
(open_shard): on-disk layout, resumable export, offline retrieval."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from functools import reduce

from audit_chain import (
    combine_proofs,
    open_shard,
    verify_proof,
    verify_proof_stream,
)
from audit_chain.record import canonical_json
from audit_chain.sharddir import MANIFEST_NAME
from tests._helpers import AuditTestCase
from tests.test_export_cost import _ReadMeter


class ShardDirCase(AuditTestCase):
    WINDOW = 7
    END = 52

    def _multi_segment(self) -> None:
        for i in range(20):
            self.chain.append("t", {"i": i})
            if i % 2 == 0:
                self.chain.append("u", {"i": i})
        self.chain.rotate()
        for i in range(20, 35):
            self.chain.append("t", {"i": i})
            if i % 2 == 0:
                self.chain.append("u", {"i": i})
        self.chain.rotate()
        for i in range(35, self.END):
            self.chain.append("t", {"i": i})
        self.chain.compact(2)

    def _export(self, directory: str | None = None) -> dict:
        directory = directory or os.path.join(self._tmp, "shards")
        return self.chain.export_shards_dir(
            "t", 0, self.END, self.WINDOW, directory
        )

    def _dir(self) -> str:
        return os.path.join(self._tmp, "shards")

    def _memory_shards(self) -> list[dict]:
        return list(self.chain.export_shards("t", 0, self.END, self.WINDOW))

    def _manifest(self, directory: str) -> dict:
        with open(os.path.join(directory, MANIFEST_NAME), "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
        self.assertTrue(raw.endswith(b"\n"))
        self.assertNotIn(b"\n", raw[:-1])  # exactly one compact line
        return json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8")[:-1])


class ExportShardsDirLayoutTest(ShardDirCase):
    def test_one_file_per_shard_byte_identical_to_memory(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        result = self._export()
        shards = self._memory_shards()
        self.assertEqual(result, {"shards": len(shards)})
        self.assertEqual(set(result), {"shards"})  # no other keys
        names = sorted(
            name
            for name in os.listdir(self._dir())
            if name.startswith("shard-")
        )
        self.assertEqual(len(names), len(shards))
        for index, shard in enumerate(shards):
            name = f"shard-{index:08d}.json"
            self.assertIn(name, names)
            with open(os.path.join(self._dir(), name), "rb") as handle:
                # Byte-identical to the in-memory shard's canonical form.
                self.assertEqual(handle.read(), canonical_json(shard).encode("utf-8"))

    def test_manifest_is_one_compact_line_and_self_authenticating(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        shards = self._memory_shards()
        manifest = self._manifest(self._dir())
        self.assertEqual(manifest["tenant"], "t")
        self.assertEqual((manifest["start"], manifest["end"]), (0, self.END))
        self.assertEqual(manifest["window"], self.WINDOW)
        self.assertEqual(len(manifest["shards"]), len(shards))
        for index, entry in enumerate(manifest["shards"]):
            self.assertEqual(entry["name"], f"shard-{index:08d}.json")
            self.assertEqual(
                (entry["start"], entry["end"]),
                (shards[index]["start"], shards[index]["end"]),
            )
            with open(os.path.join(self._dir(), entry["name"]), "rb") as handle:
                self.assertEqual(
                    entry["sha256"], hashlib.sha256(handle.read()).hexdigest()
                )
        # The tag authenticates the manifest body.
        body = {key: manifest[key] for key in manifest if key != "tag"}
        self.assertEqual(
            manifest["tag"],
            hashlib.sha256(canonical_json(body).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
        )

    def test_restored_directory_matches_one_shot_export(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        result = self._export()
        one_shot = verify_proof(self.chain.export_range("t", 0, self.END))
        streamed = verify_proof_stream(
            open_shard(self._dir(), i) for i in range(result["shards"])
        )
        self.assertEqual(streamed["total"], one_shot)
        self.assertTrue(streamed["total"]["ok"])
        combined = reduce(
            combine_proofs,
            [open_shard(self._dir(), i) for i in range(result["shards"])],
        )
        self.assertEqual(verify_proof(combined), one_shot)

    def test_restore_matches_after_compaction_and_archiving(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        self.chain.archive(os.path.join(self._tmp, "archive"))
        self._export()
        one_shot = verify_proof(self.chain.export_range("t", 0, self.END))
        restored = verify_proof_stream(
            open_shard(self._dir(), i)
            for i in range(self._export()["shards"])
        )
        self.assertEqual(restored["total"], one_shot)

    def test_export_does_not_touch_the_store(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        before = sorted(os.listdir(self.path))
        self._export()
        self.assertEqual(sorted(os.listdir(self.path)), before)

    def test_tenants_stay_isolated(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        for index in range(self._export()["shards"]):
            shard = open_shard(self._dir(), index)
            for window in shard["windows"]:
                for item in window["records"]:
                    self.assertEqual(item["record"]["tenant"], "t")

    def test_export_from_a_legacy_file_log(self) -> None:
        self.append_many("t", 9)
        result = self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 9, 4, self._dir())
        self.assertEqual(result, {"shards": 3})
        for index, shard in enumerate(self.chain.export_shards("t", 0, 9, 4)):
            self.assertEqual(open_shard(self._dir(), index), shard)

    def test_damage_outside_the_interval_does_not_change_it(self) -> None:
        self.append_many("t", 25)
        # Corrupt a record outside the exported interval in the log itself.
        target = json.dumps({"i": 24}, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)
        forged = json.dumps({"i": 99}, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)
        self.replace_in_file(target.encode(), forged.encode())
        result = self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 20, 7, self._dir())
        self.assertEqual(result, {"shards": 3})
        restored = verify_proof_stream(
            open_shard(self._dir(), i) for i in range(3)
        )
        self.assertTrue(restored["total"]["ok"])
        self.assertEqual(
            restored["total"],
            verify_proof(self.chain.export_range("t", 0, 20)),
        )

    def test_disk_and_memory_shards_splice_identically(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        memory = self._memory_shards()
        disk = [open_shard(self._dir(), i) for i in range(len(memory))]
        # A shard read back from disk is content-equal to its in-memory
        # form, so splicing never depends on which side came from disk.
        mixed = reduce(
            combine_proofs,
            [disk[i] if i % 2 == 0 else memory[i] for i in range(len(memory))],
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            verify_proof(mixed), verify_proof(self.chain.export_range("t", 0, self.END))
        )
        # Associativity is preserved over the persisted shards.
        left_assoc = reduce(combine_proofs, disk)
        right_assoc = disk[0]
        for shard in disk[1:]:
            right_assoc = combine_proofs(right_assoc, shard)
        self.assertEqual(verify_proof(left_assoc), verify_proof(right_assoc))

    def test_verdicts_agree_across_offline_batch_and_cli(self) -> None:
        from audit_chain import verify_proofs

        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        count = self._export()["shards"]
        shards = [open_shard(self._dir(), i) for i in range(count)]
        combined = reduce(combine_proofs, shards)
        offline = verify_proof(combined)
        (batch,) = verify_proofs([combined])
        self.assertEqual(
            (offline["ok"], offline["first_bad"], offline["count"]),
            (batch["ok"], batch["first_bad"], batch["count"]),
        )
        proof_file = os.path.join(self._tmp, "proof.json")
        with open(proof_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(combined, handle)
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "audit_chain", "verify-proof", proof_file],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
        )
        self.assertEqual(proc.returncode, 0)
        cli = json.loads(proc.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(
            cli,
            {
                "ok": offline["ok"],
                "first_bad": offline["first_bad"],
                "count": offline["count"],
            },
        )


class ExportShardsDirResumeTest(ShardDirCase):
    def test_complete_resume_rewrites_nothing(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        before = {
            name: os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(self._dir(), name))
            for name in os.listdir(self._dir())
        }
        result = self._export()
        self.assertEqual(result, {"shards": len(self._memory_shards())})
        after = {
            name: os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(self._dir(), name))
            for name in os.listdir(self._dir())
        }
        self.assertEqual(before, after)

    def test_interrupted_export_resumes_from_the_committed_prefix(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        shards = self._memory_shards()
        directory = self._dir()
        os.makedirs(directory)
        # Simulate a kill after two committed shards: two shard files and
        # a manifest vouching for exactly them.
        entries = []
        manifest = {
            "version": 1,
            "tenant": "t",
            "start": 0,
            "end": self.END,
            "window": self.WINDOW,
            "shards": entries,
        }
        from audit_chain import sharddir as sd

        for index in range(2):
            raw = canonical_json(shards[index]).encode("utf-8")
            sd.write_shard(directory, sd.shard_name(index), raw)
            entries.append(
                {
                    "name": sd.shard_name(index),
                    "start": shards[index]["start"],
                    "end": shards[index]["end"],
                    "sha256": hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
                }
            )
            sd.save_manifest(directory, manifest)
        committed_mtimes = {
            entry["name"]: os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(directory, entry["name"]))
            for entry in entries
        }

        result = self._export()
        self.assertEqual(result, {"shards": len(shards)})
        # The committed prefix was not rewritten.
        for name, mtime in committed_mtimes.items():
            self.assertEqual(
                os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(directory, name)), mtime
            )
        for index, shard in enumerate(shards):
            self.assertEqual(open_shard(directory, index), shard)

    def test_missing_shard_file_is_refilled(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        shards = self._memory_shards()
        victim = os.path.join(self._dir(), "shard-00000002.json")
        os.remove(victim)
        result = self._export()
        self.assertEqual(result, {"shards": len(shards)})
        self.assertEqual(open_shard(self._dir(), 2), shards[2])

    def test_stale_temp_files_are_reaped(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        junk = os.path.join(self._dir(), ".shard-00000003.json.123.4.tmp")
        with open(junk, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(b"half-written")
        self._export()
        self.assertNotIn(os.path.basename(junk), os.listdir(self._dir()))

    def test_killed_export_leaves_old_or_new_state_and_resumes(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        directory = self._dir()
        script = (
            "import sys;"
            "sys.path.insert(0, %r);"
            "from audit_chain import Chain;"
            "Chain(%r).export_shards_dir('t', 0, %d, %d, %r)"
            % (os.getcwd(), self.path, self.END, self.WINDOW, directory)
        )
        env = dict(os.environ)
        env["AUDIT_CHAIN_CRASH"] = "atomic:shard-00000003.json:before_replace"
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-c", script],
            env=env,
            capture_output=True,
        )
        self.assertNotEqual(proc.returncode, 0)  # hard-killed mid-export
        # Whatever the kill left behind, a fresh call completes the export
        # and the result matches the uninterrupted one.
        result = self._export()
        self.assertEqual(result, {"shards": len(self._memory_shards())})
        for index, shard in enumerate(self._memory_shards()):
            self.assertEqual(open_shard(directory, index), shard)
        leftovers = [
            name
            for name in os.listdir(directory)
            if name.startswith(".") and name.endswith(".tmp")
        ]
        self.assertEqual(leftovers, [])

    def test_resume_reads_only_the_missing_increment(self) -> None:
        for i in range(52):
            self.chain.append("t", {"i": i})
            if (i + 1) % 13 == 0:
                self.chain.rotate()
        self.assertTrue(self.chain.verify("t")["ok"])  # warm the cache
        self._export()
        # Shard 2 holds records 14..20, all inside the second segment.
        os.remove(os.path.join(self._dir(), "shard-00000002.json"))
        seg_files = {
            os.path.abspath(os.path.join(self.path, name))
            for name in self.segment_files()
        }
        self.assertGreater(len(seg_files), 2)
        meter = _ReadMeter()
        meter.install()
        try:
            self._export()
        finally:
            meter.remove()
        # The refill opens only the one segment covering the missing
        # shard, never the rest of the history.
        opened_segments = meter.paths & seg_files
        self.assertEqual(len(opened_segments), 1)


class ExportShardsDirErrorTest(ShardDirCase):
    def test_bad_window_and_range_raise_value_error(self) -> None:
        self.append_many("t", 10)
        for window in (0, -1, 1.5, "4", None, True):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError, msg=repr(window)):
                self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 10, window, self._dir())
        for start, end in ((0, 0), (4, 4), (9, 4), (-1, 4), (0, 11), (15, 20)):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError, msg=(start, end)):
                self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", start, end, 3, self._dir())
        for start, end in ((0.0, 4), (0, "4"), (None, 4), (True, 4)):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError, msg=(start, end)):
                self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", start, end, 3, self._dir())

    def test_bad_argument_types_raise_type_error(self) -> None:
        self.append_many("t", 4)
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.chain.export_shards_dir(42, 0, 4, 2, self._dir())
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 4, 2, 42)

    def test_empty_history_raises_value_error(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 1, 1, self._dir())

    def test_rejected_export_creates_no_directory(self) -> None:
        self.append_many("t", 4)
        target = self._dir()
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 99, 2, target)
        self.assertFalse(os.path.exists(target))

    def test_target_that_is_not_a_directory_raises_value_error(self) -> None:
        self.append_many("t", 4)
        target = os.path.join(self._tmp, "a-file")
        with open(target, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write("x")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 4, 2, target)

    def test_unparseable_manifest_raises_value_error(self) -> None:
        self.append_many("t", 4)
        directory = self._dir()
        os.makedirs(directory)
        with open(os.path.join(directory, MANIFEST_NAME), "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(b"not json\n")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 4, 2, directory)

    def test_tampered_manifest_raises_value_error(self) -> None:
        self.append_many("t", 6)
        self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 6, 2, self._dir())
        manifest = self._manifest(self._dir())
        manifest["window"] = 99  # tag no longer matches
        with open(os.path.join(self._dir(), MANIFEST_NAME), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps(manifest) + "\n")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 6, 2, self._dir())

    def test_manifest_for_a_different_export_raises_value_error(self) -> None:
        self.append_many("t", 12)
        self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 12, 3, self._dir())
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 12, 4, self._dir())  # window
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 9, 3, self._dir())  # interval
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.chain.export_shards_dir("u", 0, 12, 3, self._dir())  # tenant

    def test_existing_shard_mismatching_manifest_raises_value_error(self) -> None:
        self.append_many("t", 6)
        self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 6, 2, self._dir())
        with open(os.path.join(self._dir(), "shard-00000001.json"), "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(b"rewritten behind the manifest")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.chain.export_shards_dir("t", 0, 6, 2, self._dir())


class OpenShardTest(ShardDirCase):
    def test_random_access_single_shard(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        shards = self._memory_shards()
        # Any shard, in any order, without touching the others.
        for index in (3, 0, len(shards) - 1, 1):
            self.assertEqual(open_shard(self._dir(), index), shards[index])
            self.assertTrue(verify_proof(open_shard(self._dir(), index))["ok"])

    def test_missing_directory_and_shard_raise_file_not_found(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        with self.assertRaises(FileNotFoundError):
            open_shard(os.path.join(self._tmp, "no-such-dir"), 0)
        self._export()
        os.remove(os.path.join(self._dir(), "shard-00000001.json"))
        with self.assertRaises(FileNotFoundError):
            open_shard(self._dir(), 1)

    def test_index_out_of_range_raises_value_error(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        result = self._export()
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            open_shard(self._dir(), result["shards"])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            open_shard(self._dir(), -1)

    def test_non_integer_index_raises_type_error(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        for bad in ("0", 0.0, None, True):
            with self.assertRaises(TypeError, msg=repr(bad)):
                open_shard(self._dir(), bad)

    def test_unparseable_shard_raises_value_error(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        # Rewrite a shard and re-sign the manifest so the bytes authenticate
        # but the content is not a parseable shard.
        from audit_chain import sharddir as sd

        directory = self._dir()
        manifest = sd.load_manifest(directory)
        raw = b"[1, 2, 3]"
        with open(os.path.join(directory, "shard-00000000.json"), "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(raw)
        manifest["shards"][0]["sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
        sd.save_manifest(directory, manifest)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            open_shard(directory, 0)

    def test_shard_mismatching_manifest_raises_value_error(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        with open(os.path.join(self._dir(), "shard-00000000.json"), "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(b"tampered")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            open_shard(self._dir(), 0)

    def test_tampered_manifest_raises_value_error(self) -> None:
        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        manifest = self._manifest(self._dir())
        manifest["shards"][0]["sha256"] = "0" * 64
        with open(os.path.join(self._dir(), MANIFEST_NAME), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(json.dumps(manifest) + "\n")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            open_shard(self._dir(), 0)

    def test_open_shard_never_opens_the_log(self) -> None:
        import shutil

        self._multi_segment()
        self._export()
        shards = self._memory_shards()
        shutil.rmtree(self.path)

134	    try:
135	        fd = os.open(directory, flags)
136	    except OSError:
137	        return
138	    try:
139	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
140	            os.fsync(fd)
141	    finally:
142	        os.close(fd)

145	def verify_windows(path: str, parts: list[dict]) -> bool:
146	    """Verify retained byte windows (parts) cover the whole file.
147	
148	    The file size must equal the windows' total and each window's sha256
149	    must match. Used for sealed (never-growing) segments.
150	    """
151	    actual_size = os.path.getsize(path)
152	    return actual_size == sum(part["size"] for part in parts) and verify_prefix_windows(
153	        path, parts
154	    )

157	def verify_prefix_windows(path: str, parts: list[dict]) -> bool:
158	    """Verify the leading byte windows of ``path``; trailing bytes allowed.
159	
160	    A merged segment keeps the size and sha256 of every source segment as
161	    verification material; the merged bytes are the exact concatenation of
162	    those windows, so one streaming read re-checks every source segment. An
163	    active (still growing) segment uses the same check against its preserved
164	    prefix windows.
165	    """
166	    if not parts:
167	        return True
168	    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
169	        for part in parts:
170	            h = hashlib.sha256()
171	            remaining = part["size"]
172	            while remaining:
173	                chunk = handle.read(min(_CHUNK, remaining))
174	                if not chunk:
175	                    return False
176	                h.update(chunk)
177	                remaining -= len(chunk)
178	            if h.hexdigest() != part["sha256"]:
179	                return False
180	    return True

183	class Layout:
184	    """Resolved view of where the log data, lock and cache live."""
185	
186	    def __init__(self, root: str, kind: str):
187	        self.root = root
188	        self.kind = kind  # "dir" or "file"
189	        # The lock is a sibling dotfile in both layouts, so its identity is
190	        # stable across the file -> segment-store migration.
191	        normalized = os.path.normpath(root)
192	        parent = os.path.dirname(normalized) or "."
193	        self.lock_path = os.path.join(
194	            parent, "." + os.path.basename(normalized) + LOCK_SUFFIX
195	        )
196	        if kind == "dir":
197	            self.data_dir = root
198	            self.manifest_path = os.path.join(root, MANIFEST_NAME)
199	            self.cache_dir = root
200	            self.cache_name = CACHE_NAME
201	        else:
202	            directory = os.path.dirname(root) or "."
203	            self.data_dir = directory
204	            self.manifest_path = ""
205	            self.cache_dir = directory
206	            self.cache_name = "." + os.path.basename(root) + ".verify-cache"
207	
208	    @property

210	        return os.path.join(self.cache_dir, self.cache_name)

213	        return os.path.join(self.data_dir, name)

216	def resolve_existing(path: str) -> Optional[Layout]:
217	    """Resolve an existing log path, or return None when nothing is there."""
218	    if os.path.isdir(path):
219	        return Layout(path, "dir")
220	    if os.path.isfile(path):
221	        return Layout(path, "file")

226	# Cross-platform process-shared file locking
227	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

230	@contextlib.contextmanager
231	def file_lock(lock_path: str, *, timeout: Optional[float], shared: bool) -> Iterator[None]:
232	    """Serialize access to one log behind a process-shared OS file lock.
233	
234	    Readers take a shared lock and the writer an exclusive one. The backing
235	    primitive is chosen per platform at call time (``fcntl.flock`` on POSIX,
236	    ``LockFileEx`` on Windows), so this module imports cleanly everywhere.
237	
238	    A timeout that elapses raises ``TimeoutError`` (an ``OSError`` subclass);
239	    permission failures and path-class system errors propagate as their
240	    native ``OSError`` subclasses -- callers signal all of them silently via
241	    exit code two.
242	    """
243	    if sys.platform == "win32":  # pragma: win32 cover
244	        backend = _windows_lock
245	    else:
246	        backend = _posix_lock
247	
248	    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
249	    acquired = False
250	    try:
251	        backend(fd, shared=shared, timeout=timeout)
252	        acquired = True
253	        yield
254	    finally:
255	        if acquired:
256	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
257	                _unlock(fd)
258	        os.close(fd)

260	
261	def _posix_lock(fd: int, *, shared: bool, timeout: Optional[float]) -> None:
262	    import fcntl
263	
264	    mode = fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX
265	    if timeout is None:
266	        fcntl.flock(fd, mode)
267	        return
268	    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
269	    while True:
270	        try:
271	            fcntl.flock(fd, mode | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
272	            return
273	        except BlockingIOError:
274	            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
275	                raise TimeoutError(f"audit log lock busy: fd {fd}")
276	            time.sleep(_LOCK_POLL_SECONDS)
277	
278	
279	def _unlock(fd: int) -> None:
280	    if sys.platform == "win32":  # pragma: win32 cover
281	        _windows_unlock(fd)
282	    else:
283	        import fcntl
284	
285	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)

288	def _windows_lock(fd: int, *, shared: bool, timeout: Optional[float]) -> None:  # pragma: win32 cover
289	    import ctypes
290	    from ctypes import wintypes
291	
292	    import msvcrt
293	
294	    LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK = 0x00000002
295	    LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY = 0x00000001
296	    ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION = 33
297	
298	    class _Overlapped(ctypes.Structure):
299	        _fields_ = [
300	            ("Internal", ctypes.c_void_p),
301	            ("InternalHigh", ctypes.c_void_p),
302	            ("Offset", wintypes.DWORD),
303	            ("OffsetHigh", wintypes.DWORD),
304	            ("hEvent", wintypes.HANDLE),
305	        ]
306	
307	    kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
308	    lock_file_ex = kernel32.LockFileEx
309	    lock_file_ex.restype = wintypes.BOOL
310	    lock_file_ex.argtypes = [
311	        wintypes.HANDLE,
312	        wintypes.DWORD,
313	        wintypes.DWORD,
314	        wintypes.DWORD,
315	        wintypes.DWORD,
316	        ctypes.POINTER(_Overlapped),
317	    ]
318	
319	    handle = msvcrt.get_osfhandle(fd)
320	    flags = LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY if timeout is not None else 0
321	    if not shared:
322	        flags |= LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK
323	    deadline = None if timeout is None else time.monotonic() + timeout
324	    while True:
325	        overlapped = _Overlapped()
326	        if lock_file_ex(handle, flags, 0, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, ctypes.byref(overlapped)):
327	            return
328	        error = ctypes.get_last_error()
329	        if error != ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION:
330	            raise OSError(error, f"LockFileEx failed (error {error})")
331	        if deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline:
332	            raise TimeoutError(f"audit log lock busy: fd {fd}")
333	        time.sleep(_LOCK_POLL_SECONDS)

343	        _fields_ = [
344	            ("Internal", ctypes.c_void_p),
345	            ("InternalHigh", ctypes.c_void_p),
346	            ("Offset", wintypes.DWORD),
347	            ("OffsetHigh", wintypes.DWORD),
348	            ("hEvent", wintypes.HANDLE),
349	        ]
350	
351	    kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)

353	    unlock_file_ex.argtypes = [
354	        wintypes.HANDLE,
355	        wintypes.DWORD,
356	        wintypes.DWORD,
357	        wintypes.DWORD,
358	        ctypes.POINTER(_Overlapped),
359	    ]

373	# Manifest (self-authenticating, atomically replaced)
374	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
375	
376	
377	class AuditMetadataError(ValueError):
378	    """A tampered manifest or verify cache.
379	
380	    Distinct from a malformed record line: damaged *metadata* is reported as
381	    chain corruption (verify returns ``ok=False``), whereas a half-written
382	    record keeps its existing bad-line semantics (ValueError, exit code 2).
383	    """
384	
385	
386	def default_manifest(first: str) -> dict:
387	    return {
388	        "version": 1,
389	        "active": first,
390	        "segments": [{"name": first, "sealed": False, "parts": []}],
391	    }
392	
393	
394	def _manifest_payload_text(manifest: dict) -> str:
395	    body = {
396	        "version": manifest["version"],
397	        "active": manifest["active"],
398	        "segments": manifest["segments"],
399	    }
400	    # The archive location is part of the signed body only when present, so
401	    # manifests written before two-tier storage existed keep their tags.
402	    if manifest.get("archive") is not None:
403	        body["archive"] = manifest["archive"]
404	    return rec.canonical_json(body)
405	
406	
407	def sign_manifest(manifest: dict) -> dict:
408	    """Return a manifest copy carrying its authentication tag."""
409	    signed = {
410	        "version": manifest["version"],
411	        "active": manifest["active"],
412	        "segments": manifest["segments"],
413	    }
414	    if manifest.get("archive") is not None:
415	        signed["archive"] = manifest["archive"]
416	    signed["tag"] = hashlib.sha256(
417	        _manifest_payload_text(signed).encode(_ENCODING)
418	    ).hexdigest()
419	    return signed
420	
421	
422	def load_manifest(layout: Layout) -> Optional[dict]:
423	    try:
424	        with open(layout.manifest_path, "rb") as handle:
425	            raw = handle.read()
426	    except FileNotFoundError:
427	        return None
428	    try:
429	        manifest = json.loads(raw.decode(_ENCODING))
430	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) as exc:
431	        raise AuditMetadataError("malformed audit manifest") from exc
432	    if not isinstance(manifest, dict) or not _valid_manifest(manifest):
433	        raise AuditMetadataError("malformed audit manifest")
434	    tag = manifest.get("tag")
435	    if tag is not None:
436	        if not isinstance(tag, str):
437	            raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit manifest")
438	        expected = hashlib.sha256(
439	            _manifest_payload_text(manifest).encode(_ENCODING)
440	        ).hexdigest()
441	        if not constant_time_equal(tag, expected):
442	            raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit manifest")
443	    # A manifest without a tag was written by the pre-tag build: structurally
444	    # valid and accepted read-only; the next write re-signs it.
445	    return manifest
446	
447	
448	def _valid_manifest(manifest: Any) -> bool:
449	    if not isinstance(manifest, dict):
450	        return False
451	    if manifest.get("version") != 1 or not isinstance(manifest.get("active"), str):
452	        return False
453	    archive = manifest.get("archive")
454	    if archive is not None and not isinstance(archive, str):
455	        return False
456	    segments = manifest.get("segments")
457	    if not isinstance(segments, list) or not segments:
458	        return False
459	    for index, segment in enumerate(segments):
460	        if not isinstance(segment, dict):
461	            return False
462	        if not isinstance(segment.get("name"), str) or not isinstance(
463	            segment.get("sealed"), bool
464	        ):
465	            return False
466	        archived = segment.get("archived", False)
467	        if not isinstance(archived, bool):
468	            return False
469	        if archived:
470	            # An archived segment lives in the recorded archive location; it
471	            # is always sealed and never the active segment.
472	            if not archive or not segment["sealed"]:
473	                return False
474	            if segment["name"] == manifest["active"]:
475	                return False
476	        parts = segment.get("parts")
477	        if not isinstance(parts, list):
478	            return False
479	        for part in parts:
480	            if not _valid_part(part):
481	                return False
482	        if index == len(segments) - 1:
483	            if segment["name"] != manifest["active"] or segment["sealed"]:
484	                return False
485	        elif not segment["sealed"] or not parts:
486	            return False
487	    tag = manifest.get("tag")
488	    if tag is not None and not isinstance(tag, str):
489	        return False
490	    return True
491	
492	
493	def _valid_part(part: Any) -> bool:
494	    return (
495	        isinstance(part, dict)
496	        and isinstance(part.get("name"), str)
497	        and isinstance(part.get("size"), int)
498	        and isinstance(part.get("sha256"), str)
499	    )
500	
501	
502	def save_manifest(layout: Layout, manifest: dict) -> None:
503	    save_manifest_at(layout.data_dir, manifest)
504	
505	
506	def save_manifest_at(directory: str, manifest: dict) -> None:
507	    """Write a signed manifest into an arbitrary directory (e.g. staging)."""
508	    signed = sign_manifest(manifest)
509	    atomic_write_text(directory, MANIFEST_NAME, rec.canonical_json(signed))
510

512	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
513	# Incremental verify cache
514	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
515	
516	
517	def cache_tag_payload(version: int, segments: dict) -> bytes:
518	    return rec.canonical_json({"version": version, "segments": segments}).encode(
519	        _ENCODING
520	    )
521	
522	
523	def load_cache(layout: Layout) -> Optional[dict]:
524	    """Load the verify cache or return None when absent.
525	
526	    A present cache whose authentication tag fails to verify is tampering:
527	    ``AuditMetadataError`` is raised rather than silently rebuilding, because
528	    reporting a clean pass off a forged cache must be impossible.
529	    """
530	    try:
531	        with open(layout.cache_path, "rb") as handle:
532	            raw = handle.read()
533	    except FileNotFoundError:
534	        return None
535	    try:
536	        cache = json.loads(raw.decode(_ENCODING))
537	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) as exc:
538	        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache") from exc
539	    if not isinstance(cache, dict) or cache.get("version") != 1:
540	        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache")
541	    tag = cache.get("tag")
542	    segments = cache.get("segments")
543	    if not isinstance(tag, str) or not isinstance(segments, dict):
544	        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache")
545	    expected = hashlib.sha256(cache_tag_payload(1, segments)).hexdigest()
546	    if not constant_time_equal(tag, expected):
547	        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache")
548	    if not _valid_cache_segments(segments):
549	        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache")
550	    return {"version": 1, "segments": segments, "tag": tag}
551	
552	
553	def constant_time_equal(actual: str, expected: str) -> bool:
554	    if len(actual) != len(expected):
555	        return False
556	    result = 0
557	    for a, b in zip(actual, expected):
558	        result |= ord(a) ^ ord(b)
559	    return result == 0
560	
561	
562	def _valid_cache_segments(segments: Any) -> bool:
563	    if not isinstance(segments, dict):
564	        return False
565	    for name, entry in segments.items():
566	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not isinstance(entry, dict):
567	            return False
568	        if (
569	            not isinstance(entry.get("records"), int)
570	            or entry["records"] < 0
571	            or not isinstance(entry.get("size"), int)
572	            or entry["size"] < 0
573	            or not isinstance(entry.get("mtime_ns"), int)
574	            or not isinstance(entry.get("ctime_ns"), int)
575	        ):
576	            return False
577	        parts = entry.get("parts")
578	        if not isinstance(parts, list):
579	            return False
580	        for part in parts:
581	            if not _valid_part(part):
582	                return False
583	        # The fold is absent only in a structurally-valid pre-fold cache,
584	        # which the walker rebuilds from bytes; a present but malformed fold
585	        # cannot be trusted and is treated like any forged field.
586	        fold = entry.get("fold")
587	        if fold is not None:
588	            if not isinstance(fold, str) or len(fold) != 64:
589	                return False
590	            try:
591	                int(fold, 16)
592	            except ValueError:
593	                return False
594	        tenants = entry.get("tenants")
595	        if not isinstance(tenants, dict):
596	            return False
597	        for tenant, state in tenants.items():
598	            if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not isinstance(state, list):
599	                return False
600	            if len(state) != 3:
601	                return False
602	            count, digest, bad = state
603	            if (
604	                not isinstance(count, int)
605	                or not isinstance(digest, str)
606	                or not isinstance(bad, int)
607	                or count < 0
608	                or bad < -1
609	            ):
610	                return False
611	    return True
612	
613	
614	def save_cache(layout: Layout, segments: dict) -> None:
615	    tag = hashlib.sha256(cache_tag_payload(1, segments)).hexdigest()
616	    payload = {"version": 1, "segments": segments, "tag": tag}
617	    atomic_write_text(
618	        layout.cache_dir, layout.cache_name, rec.canonical_json(payload)
619	    )
620

628	    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
629	        return handle.read()

636	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
637	        raise ValueError("malformed audit record") from exc
